stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x) = 7 - 2x\) and \(g(x) = 3x + c\), where \(c\) is a constant. In the \(xy\)-plane, the graphs of \(y = f(x)\) and \(y = g(x)\) intersect at a point on the \(x\)-axis. What is the value of \(c\)?
solution: The graph of \(f\) meets the \(x\)-axis where \(7 - 2x = 0\), so at \(x = \frac{7}{2}\).
The intersection point is \(\left(\frac{7}{2}, 0\right)\), so \(g\left(\frac{7}{2}\right) = 0\): \(\frac{21}{2} + c = 0\).
verify:
x, c = symbols('x c')
x0 = solve(7 - 2*x, x)[0]
cs = solve(Eq(3*x0 + c, 0), c)
assert cs == [Rational(-21, 2)]
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == cs
